title: BranchIP: Learning Adaptive Equivariant Computation for Interatomic Potentials
abstract: arXiv:2610.02013v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Equivariant machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have revolutionized atomistic modeling, but accurate treatment of complex materials and molecular systems demands expensive models. This limits simulation length- and time-scales, with tensor products a key computational bottleneck. The recent emergence of foundation-scale MLIPs further exacerbates this challenge. We present Branch Interatomic Potential (BranchIP), a single-model framework for learned adaptive tensor product computation, trained with a novel distillation loss. In our experiments on two systems of physical interest, a heterogeneous catalysis system and a proton-conducting solid acid electrolyte, BranchIP accelerates MLIPs across model sizes by up to $2.4\times$ while reducing memory usage by up to $2.6\times$. translated_title: BranchIP：面向原子间势的学习型自适应等变计算
translated_abstract: 等变机器学习原子间势（MLIP）已彻底改变了原子级建模领域，但对复杂材料和分子体系的精确处理需要代价高昂的模型。这限制了模拟的空间和时间尺度，其中张量积运算是关键的计算瓶颈。近来出现的基础规模MLIP进一步加剧了这一挑战。我们提出了分支原子间势，这是一个通过学习实现自适应张量积计算的单一模型框架，并采用一种新颖的蒸馏损失进行训练。在两个具有物理意义的体系——多相催化体系和质子导电固体酸电解质——上的实验表明，BranchIP可在各种模型规模下将MLIP加速高达2.4倍，同时将内存占用降低高达2.6倍，且保持了物理保真度。此外，学习到的自适应计算还提供了模型可解释性，能够揭示模型关注哪些相互作用。
tldr: BranchIP提出一种通过新颖蒸馏损失学习自适应张量积计算的单一模型框架，在保持物理保真度的前提下将等变机器学习原子间势加速高达2.4倍、内存占用降低高达2.6倍，并提供了模型可解释性。
en_tdlr: BranchIP introduces a single-model framework that learns adaptive tensor product computation via a novel distillation loss, accelerating equivariant MLIPs by up to 2.4× and reducing memory usage by up to 2.6× while preserving physical fidelity and providing model interpretability.
